title: Bubbles rounded off, and switched on by default
question: Do these read as bubbles now rather than as blocks? They are on by default from this build - say if that is a step too far and I will put it back behind the key.
context_md:
*"Off (current) and rising look best. I wish the bigger bubbles weren't so blocky."*

Both halves acted on. **RISING is the default now**, and it no longer draws squares.

A 2x2 bubble cannot be anything but a square -- every pixel of it is a corner. The site is 3x3 with the four corners left dark, which is the smallest mark on a square grid that reads as a disc.

**The shape change quietly cut the effect to a third, which is worth telling you because nothing about it was meant to touch strength.** The density knob was being applied per *site*, so a 5-of-9 disc covered 5/9 of what a 4-of-4 square did: 3,250 lit pixels became 1,125 on the same scene. It is normalised per pixel now and reads 3,200 -- same amount of boil, different shape. COLUMNS is deliberately untouched: it is a stream leaving a nucleation site rather than a bubble, and rounding it would collapse the difference between the two looks.

Costs nothing measurable: a forced full-screen redraw of this pan is 14.11 ms with them off and 14.26 with them on, against a run-to-run spread wider than that.

`H` still cycles all four, and OFF is still there as the way back.

Zoomed 6x and slowed, because rounded and square are four pixels apart -- at normal zoom you would be judging a guess.
